homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name. 'TO' and 'the Turkopticon Script' are the census's other names for the entity; 'turkopticon.ucsd.edu' (named in the FAQ) and 'turkopticon.net' are its hosts. The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT, MTurk), the platform on which it rates requesters, announced by Amazon to close on 30 September 2026 (B6 F28); Turkopticon is 'not associated with Amazon' (B8 F37)
Lilly Irani and M. Six Silberman, its founders (persons); the archive's 'Silberman' is Steve Silberman, author of NeuroTribes (#476, #1147), a third person
Tech Workers Coalition, whose volunteers maintain it (B8 F35)
DoloresLabs, the crowdsourcing company that seeded its first 300 reviews and whose reading of its purpose the founders set aside (B5 F59)
TurkerNation and mturkforum, the worker forums of 2013 (B5)
the Data Workers' Inquiry and Fairwork's Cloudwork Ratings, the census's neighbours (LV-32, LV-33); no /non row exists for either
DAIR, which the census names beside Krystal Kauffman (LV-32)
Platform Cooperativism, the channel of the video card (B7)

captures.description: TURKOPTICON, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a worker-led advocacy organization and review system created in 2008 by Lilly Irani and M. Six Silberman.' The review tool for Mechanical Turk requesters (pay, fairness, speed, communication), its purpose against invisibility (unfair rejections, wage theft) and the expansion to data workers across industries. No closing offer. Seven cards: Turkopticon's own page, the CHI 2013 paper, the 2008–2015 lessons paper, a Reddit thread on the expansion, a LinkedIn post, a video.
